actual_mcp_transport.scope:
Exercise real MCP stdio receipt boundaries using isolated daemon state.

This is transport acceptance, not an actual model or provider idle-wake trial.
steps: wait/read results retained IDs across MCP process death and reconnect
selective repeated receipt preserved newer arrivals and refused a foreign-agent argument
broken MCP output retained messages for explicit receipt after reconnect
CLI acknowledgement retained a later arrival and refused simultaneous drain

native_workflow.scope:
Exercise production Iced controls in owned fixture state, then reopen the app.

Scenarios invoke callbacks collected from the actual rendered controls. This checks
native rendering and action wiring; it is not physical keyboard or screen-reader testing.

notification_navigation.scope:
Exercise notification navigation through real desktop processes and private IPC.

This tests existing-window and cold-start routing with actual daemon state and
rendered controls. It does not simulate or claim a Notification Center click.
Native sender authorization and physical notification clicks are separate trials.

limits: MCP transport fixtures do not establish actual-provider receipt or idle wake.
The default read is now non-destructive; explicit drain=true and legacy lifecycle hooks retain their documented semantics.
Desktop dismissal acknowledges only the selected human-inbox message after a click; pending questions and drafts remain.
No installed daemon, launcher or live user provider was replaced.
Native notification permission/signing and actual Notification Center clicks remain open.
